correctness.rationale: The exact distance formula on Cartesian products yields mutual exclusion of selected columns at gaps 0 or 1. A cyclic gap >=4 makes a fully undominated rung; a gap of 2 between same rows violates packing; a gap of 3 between same rows leaves adjacent undominated vertices. One selected vertex fails including n=3. Conversely all even alternating 2/3-gap configurations satisfy both requirements, as checked by local gap inspection. Rooted cyclic gap words have exactly k possible marked starts, proving 2n/k times binomial(k,n-2k), and a formal derivative gives the rational series. Exact independent graph-enumeration tests n=3..21, mask-by-mask comparisons n=3..14, and a 120-term recurrence check corroborate all boundaries; no finite check substitutes for the universal proof. value.rationale: The 2026 graph-theory source introduces packing-isolating sets, establishes general tree existence and gives nonexistence examples beyond trees. Circular ladders are a natural cubic cyclic test family. The new structural bijection gives an exact all-order, all-cardinality enumeration, the rational generating function, the precise exceptional circumference 7 amid positive neighboring circumferences, and all supported minimum and maximum sizes. These conclusions are not routine single-number computations or arbitrary small slices, and are not implied by known ordinary packing or edge-isolation bounds. The finite checker and reproducibility are distinct support for C, not a substitute for this graph-theoretic motivation.
